Two different mechanisms, easy to conflate:

## 1. Scripts that hook the worktree lifecycle (per-project)

Scripts live in **Project settings → Scripts** (or global defaults), and can be checked into the repo as `t3.json` at the repo root. Each script is `{name, command, icon?, runOnWorktreeCreate?, runOnSettle?, async?, previewUrl?, autoOpenPreview?}`.

The lifecycle hooks:

| field | when it runs | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `runOnWorktreeCreate` | right after a worktree is created for a new thread | only the **first** matching script runs (`scripts.find(s => s.runOnWorktreeCreate)`) |
| `async` | — | `runOnWorktreeCreate` only. Default `true`: agent starts while setup still runs. `false`: the agent is held until the script exits (failure → "Worktree ready, setup script failed", queued messages stay held) |
| `runOnSettle` | every time the thread settles, inside the thread's worktree | also first-match only; threads on the project checkout (no own worktree) skip it. This is your teardown hook (e.g. delete build output) |

Setup/settle scripts get `T3CODE_PROJECT_ROOT` (project root) and `T3CODE_WORKTREE_PATH` (the thread's worktree) in their env, and run in a T3 Code terminal.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://t3.codes/schema/t3.json",
  "defaultThreadEnvMode": "worktree",
  "worktreeSubmodules": "recursive",
  "scripts": [
    {
      "name": "Setup",
      "command": "mise install && pnpm install",
      "icon": "play",
      "runOnWorktreeCreate": true,
      "async": false
    },
    {
      "name": "Clean",
      "command": "rm -rf .next dist coverage",
      "runOnSettle": true
    },
    {
      "name": "Dev",
      "command": "pnpm dev",
      "previewUrl": "http://localhost:3000",
      "autoOpenPreview": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Max 50 scripts. `t3.json` scripts are what everyone opening the repo gets; a project-level override in the app (`projectSettingsOverrides[<projectId>].defaultProjectScripts`) wins, otherwise repo scripts win over the global `defaultProjectScripts`.

## 2. Worktree retention/cleanup (not a script — app setting)

`worktreeCleanup` is a separate setting, in **Settings → Storage/Worktrees** or `~/.t3/userdata/settings.json` (with a per-project override):

```json
"worktreeCleanup": {
  "mode": "custom",
  "rules": {
    "worktreeKeepWhen": "uncommitted-changes",   // any-local-files | uncommitted-changes | tracked-changes
    "worktreeAfterDays": null,
    "worktreeSettledAfterDays": 7,
    "worktreeOnMerge": true,
    "worktreeOnDelete": true,
    "worktreeUnchanged": false
  }
}
```

`mode: "off"` disables it. Note `t3.json` only accepts `defaultThreadEnvMode`, `worktreeSubmodules`, `iconPath`, and `scripts` — cleanup rules are not repo-configurable.

There is no "on worktree delete" script hook; `runOnSettle` plus the cleanup rules cover that side.

- `runOnWorktreeCreate: true` — the only setup hook; runs once per new thread worktree, cwd = the worktree, so `cp` lands in the right place.

- Both guards matter: no source file (fresh clone on another machine) → skip with a message instead of a failed setup; existing file in the worktree → don't clobber local edits.
